A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with LAFO renamed ORA. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support matching retained content against the additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet detection results, ensemble experiments, activation-shaping experiments, and centering and aggregation ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds multi-backbone, CLIP, near-OOD, MobileNet, and MNIST/Fashion-MNIST experiments.

M1.justification: The core projection, ID-mean centering, maximum-angle score, and ensemble summation remain unchanged. Section 4.2 adds a limited zero-shot CLIP adaptation that constructs decision boundaries from class-text embeddings and projects normalized features without fitting a linear probe.

E1.justification: The original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet benchmark coverage is retained. Appendix I adds NINCO and SSB-Hard, extending evaluation to semantically similar near-OOD examples. Appendix K adds MNIST training and MNIST versus Fashion-MNIST evaluation, substantially broadening the represented data and test scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparators including MaxLogit, R-Mah, R-Cos, P-Cos, NNGuide, NCI, and NECO in Table 1, plus MCM in the CLIP comparison. Tables 10–11 newly compare standalone ReAct against ORA and their combination. The original benchmark comparator sets remain in Tables 8–9.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a nine-backbone ImageNet evaluation, including ImageNet-21k-pretrained variants, CLIP ViT-H/14 linear-probe and zero-shot protocols, MobileNetV2 evaluation, and a trained LeNet-5 experiment. The original FPR95/AUROC metrics and 10,000-sample CIFAR-10 and 50,000-sample ImageNet evaluation sets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the original ablations, v2 tests individual class anchors, elementwise minimum and median centering, and summed scores from multiple reference points. It adds explicit non-contrastive model comparisons, angle-component histograms in Figure 6, and a MNIST/Fashion-MNIST test of the boundary-distance premise in Table 21.

E5.justification: Table 21 newly reports standard deviations and ranges of sample-to-boundary distances, alongside means. These describe variation across samples, not uncertainty across training runs. Both versions retain the deterministic-given-checkpoint statement and provide no repeated-run confidence intervals or significance tests for detection performance.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, ensemble, activation-shaping, and principal ablation numbers are retained. v2 adds substantial results, including 38.34% average FPR95 across nine backbones, CLIP zero-shot/linear-probe FPR95 of 25.85%/23.94%, and near-OOD, MobileNet, and expanded ablation results. These are additional settings, not gains over the retained same-setting results.

T1.justification: The original geometric equations and law-of-sines relation remain. Appendix C adds a proof of the existing scale-invariance claim under positive encoder scaling and a shared bias-free head; Section 4.2 derives the CLIP boundary projection. These are bounded extensions of the existing geometry. New Appendix J also introduces angle-vertex labels inconsistent with Equation 2.

C1.justification: v2 shifts the abstract and contributions toward best average performance across nine backbones, five backbone wins, universal top-three rankings, and CLIP applicability. The explicit linear-scaling contribution is dropped. These materially broaden the empirical claims, although Table 1 actually shows four wins and fifth-place results on Swin and EVA.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive near-OOD applicability qualifications and explanations of why class-centroid methods may handle subtle shifts better. It extends the contrastive-feature interpretation to CLIP, adds a cross-entropy feature-alignment explanation in Appendix K, and proposes variance- or accuracy-weighted class anchors in Appendix L. The original mean-only limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds timm checkpoint sources for the new backbones and identifies the LAION CLIP ViT-H/14 checkpoint. The existing PyTorch/H100 setup, original checkpoint sources, and activation-shaping percentiles remain. Implementation disclosure expands modestly; detailed training settings for the new linear probes and LeNet experiment are still missing.

R1.justification: Related work adds NNGuide, relative Mahalanobis, and centroid-based cosine methods P-Cos/R-Cos, while dropping the DICE and GradOrth discussion. References also expand for CLIP, newer architectures, and near-OOD benchmarks. The central positioning as a post-hoc geometric detector closest to fDBD remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative around multi-backbone ImageNet and CLIP evaluation. Original benchmark discussion and pseudocode move into appendices, which are reorganized into Sections A–L. The abstract and contribution list are rewritten, and the title, method terminology, and citation style change throughout.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document template and substantially restructures the displays: original benchmark tables move to the appendix, activation-shaping results receive separate summary and detailed tables, and the ensemble display is relabeled as a table. Numerous new comparison tables and an angle-component histogram grid are added; original distribution plots are retained with renamed axes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mainly ResNet-based validation, v2 adds valuable architecture, CLIP, near-OOD, and ablation evidence plus a scale-invariance proof. However, its new headline ranking claims contradict Table 1: four wins, not five, and fifth place on Swin and EVA. ORA's plain ResNet-50 FPR95 also differs across Tables 1, 18, and 4 (43.63, 49.32, and 44.58) without clear setting distinctions. These material reporting problems affect the central evidence, preventing a confident net quality judgment despite the substantial additions.
